biography.plain_text: Thomas Sackville-Manning was a British brewer and chairman of Southdown and East Grinstead Breweries. He and his father, Augustus, acquired breweries in Sussex and brought their interests together in the company. Born in Surbiton, he lived at Brewery House in East Grinstead and also served as a director of Fremlins.

long_biography.plain_text:
Thomas Sackville-Manning sold Southdown and East Grinstead Breweries to Tamplins in 1924 and joined the buyer's board. The transaction was valued at £274,075. Tamplins retained the South Malling malthouse to replace an older facility in Brighton, while the former brewery premises in Lewes and East Grinstead were sold off.

Educated at Cheltenham College and Cambridge University, Manning also served as a magistrate and spent five seasons on Sussex County Cricket Club's governing committee. His property interests included a brief period of ownership of Malling Deanery, which he sold to the businessman Sir Frank Sanderson in 1920.
